newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Mandela to join AIDS session at global forum.
newsitem.headline: Mandela to join AIDS session at global forum.

text.p: South Africa's President Nelson Mandela will attend the coming World Economic Forum in Davos to take part in a discussion on AIDS, organisers said on Tuesday.
Also joining the session, to be held on Monday as the week-long gathering of global political and business leaders winds to a close, will be U.S. Secretary of Health Donna Shalala.
South Africa has reported a surge in cases of AIDS, or Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome, which the United Nations says now affects 22.6 million people around the globe.
Last November the world body's UNAIDS agency said sub-Saharan Africa was one of the worst-hit regions, with 14 million or 63 per cent of the total.

Between 1994 and 1996, UNAIDS said, the number of pregnant women infected with the HIV virus, which most researchers say leads to AIDS, tripled from one in 25 to one in 10 in South Africa's Free State province.
In Kwazulu-Natal, the agency added, the rate doubled from one in 10 to one in five.

Joining Mandela and Shalala at the Davos discussion will be UNAIDS chief Peter Piot, and Sir Richard Sykes, chief executive officer of Britain's Glaxo Welcome company which is active in AIDS research.

The Forum's programme this year ranges over issues like the effect of globalisation on workers in the richer countries, prospects for continuing expansion of emerging economies, and the outlook for European monetary union.

Other top leaders due to attend include new U.N. Secretary- General Kofi Annan, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin of Russia, President Hosni Mubarak of Egypt, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat.

Diplomats said Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas, who is among a long list of senior political figures going to the annual gathering in the Swiss mountain resort, will have talks there with Annan on the East Timor problem.
The U.N. has never recognised Indonesia's absorption of the former Portuguese colony in 1976 after invading in 1975 and has sponsored long-running talks between Jakarta and Lisbon on the issue.
